plan.planning_summary: Refining route_01 (Ge/ZnS Fabry-Perot dual-bandpass) based on iteration_13 results showing 0.960 target score with 24-layer three-cavity design. Previous iteration_05 achieved 0.978 with 20-layer two-cavity, suggesting optimization may benefit from different strategies. Three complementary routes proposed: (1) differential evolution optimizer with wider bounds to escape local minima, (2) 22-layer intermediate topology balancing complexity and performance, (3) alternative material pair PbTe/ZnS for different index contrast. All routes maintain parent_route_id: route_01 per refinement chain requirement.

routes.title: Ge/ZnS Three-Cavity Fabry-Perot with Differential Evolution Optimizer
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Differential evolution global optimizer will escape local minima that gradient descent encountered in iteration_13, achieving higher target score by exploring thickness space more thoroughly while maintaining the three-cavity Fabry-Perot topology.
routes.design_principle: Multi-cavity Fabry-Perot bandpass filter with computational optimization using global search rather than local gradient methods. Three cavities enable square passband profile with strong out-of-band blocking.
routes.proposed_topology: CaF2 substrate | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Air (24 layers total, alternating Ge/ZnS starting with Ge)
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 4150-4350 nm band
maximize mean transmittance in 4550-4750 nm band
minimize mean transmittance in 3600-4000 nm band
minimize mean transmittance in 4850-5200 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: conventional IR dielectric materials Ge and ZnS are depositable
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack with computational optimization principle from evidence
Multi-cavity Fabry-Perot enables square passband profile
expected_advantages: Global optimizer explores thickness space more thoroughly than gradient descent
May find better local minima than iteration_13's gradient-based result
Maintains proven Ge/ZnS material pair with high index contrast
known_risks: Differential evolution requires more function evaluations
May still converge to similar local minimum if landscape is rugged
Global search does not guarantee better solution
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer infrared bandpass filter on CaF2 substrate with alternating Ge and ZnS layers (Ge first, ZnS second, repeating for 24 total layers). Wavelength bands: passbands at 4150-4350 nm and 4550-4750 nm, stopbands at 3600-4000 nm and 4850-5200 nm. Normal incidence, unpolarized light, coherent TMM. Initialize all layer thicknesses to 550 nm for Ge and 900 nm for ZnS (quarter-wave at ~4500 nm). Optimization bounds: 200-1500 nm for all layers. Use differential_evolution_thickness optimizer with population size 50, max generations 200. Objective: maximize weighted sum of mean transmittance in both passbands minus mean transmittance in both stopbands. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
routes.revision_reason: Changed optimizer from gradient_thickness (iteration_13) to differential_evolution_thickness to escape local minima and explore thickness space more globally while maintaining same 24-layer Ge/ZnS topology.

routes.title: Ge/ZnS Two-Cavity Fabry-Perot with 22 Layers and Asymmetric Initialization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Reducing from 24 to 22 layers with asymmetric cavity thickness initialization will simplify the optimization landscape while maintaining dual-bandpass performance, potentially achieving higher target score than iteration_13's three-cavity design by reducing degrees of freedom that cause local minima.
routes.design_principle: Two-cavity Fabry-Perot with intermediate layer count balances performance and optimization tractability. Asymmetric initialization breaks symmetry to help optimizer distinguish cavity roles for dual-band operation.
routes.proposed_topology: CaF2 substrate | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Air (22 layers total, alternating Ge/ZnS starting with Ge)
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 4150-4350 nm band
maximize mean transmittance in 4550-4750 nm band
minimize mean transmittance in 3600-4000 nm band
minimize mean transmittance in 4850-5200 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: Ge and ZnS are conventional IR dielectrics
theory_basis: Bandwidth depends on layer count from evidence
Two-cavity design demonstrated in prior literature for NDIR sensors
expected_advantages: Iteration_05 showed 20-layer achieved 0.978, suggesting 22-layer may bridge 20 and 24 performance
Asymmetric initialization may help optimizer find dual-band solution more easily
known_risks: Fewer cavities may reduce stopband blocking performance
May not achieve as square passband profile as three-cavity design
Intermediate layer count may not offer clear advantage

Wavelength bands: passbands at 4150-4350 nm and 4550-4750 nm, stopbands at 3600-4000 nm and 4850-5200 nm. Normal incidence, unpolarized light, coherent TMM. routes.revision_reason: Changed layer count from 24 (iteration_13) to 22 layers with asymmetric thickness initialization to test whether intermediate complexity improves optimization convergence while maintaining dual-bandpass performance.

routes.title: PbTe/ZnS Three-Cavity Fabry-Perot with 24 Layers
routes.scientific_hypothesis: PbTe/ZnS material pair will achieve different refractive index contrast compared to Ge/ZnS, potentially enabling better dual-bandpass performance with stronger stopband blocking due to PbTe's higher index in mid-IR range while maintaining low absorption.
routes.design_principle: Multi-cavity Fabry-Perot bandpass filter with alternative high-index material PbTe paired with low-index ZnS. Higher index contrast may enable stronger reflectivity per layer pair, improving stopband blocking with same layer count.
routes.proposed_topology: CaF2 substrate | PbTe | ZnS | PbTe | ZnS | PbTe | ZnS | PbTe | ZnS | PbTe | ZnS | PbTe | ZnS | PbTe | ZnS | PbTe | ZnS | PbTe | ZnS | PbTe | ZnS | PbTe | ZnS | PbTe | ZnS | Air (24 layers total, alternating PbTe/ZnS starting with PbTe)
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 4150-4350 nm band
maximize mean transmittance in 4550-4750 nm band
minimize mean transmittance in 3600-4000 nm band
minimize mean transmittance in 4850-5200 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: PbTe and ZnS are conventional depositable IR dielectrics
theory_basis: High-low index material pair selection principle from evidence
Index contrast affects reflectivity per layer pair
expected_advantages: PbTe may provide higher index contrast than Ge in mid-IR
Different material dispersion may improve dual-band separation
Tests material sensitivity of the design approach
known_risks: PbTe absorption characteristics in target bands must be verified by solver
Material may have higher absorption than Ge reducing peak transmittance
Different thermal expansion may affect manufacturing (not modeled in TMM)
